request.what: Fund a 12-month Governance Incentives Framework project to research, model, test, dashboard, and propose governance incentive mechanisms for Cardano.

claims.claim: The proposal requests ₳4,207,967 for a 12-month Governance Incentives Framework project covering research, data, modeling, community engagement, dashboarding, pilot testing, and governance integration.
The document says Cardano currently lacks a structured, data-driven framework for determining how governance contributions should be incentivized, measured, or supported over time.
The document cites early governance data showing active DReps declined in every 12-epoch period, the DRep Gini coefficient rose from 0.92 to 0.94, and 11-16 DReps represent 51% of voting power.
The document says the State of Governance research identified an incentive deficit as a major structural barrier and that one Constitutional Committee consortium retired due to lack of compensation.

The project commits to evaluate incentive mechanisms for participation quality, reward distribution, concentration risk, accountability, delegator effects, gaming risk, and budget sustainability rather than treating turnout alone as success.
The milestones describe seven staged work packages from discovery through final reporting, with public outputs and acceptance criteria for each stage.
The proposal includes a controlled incentive pilot intended to test one clearly defined experiment and publish methodology, results, deviations, limitations, and implications.

The proposal sets KPIs including 50+ governance actors engaged, 10+ workshops, 12 monthly updates, 50+ simulation scenarios, at least 99% monitoring availability, under one-hour data latency, 5+ dashboards, and 95% timeline adherence.
The budget is presented only at workstream level, while the detailed operational budget is stated to be maintained separately for audit, administration, and delivery management.
The team section asserts prior Cardano governance, Catalyst, research, ambassador, consulting, and project closeout experience for Seomon, Sebastian Pereira, and Cerkoryn.

summary: The document presents a large 12-month treasury-funded R&D program for governance incentives, with clear high-level deliverables, milestones, and KPIs, but it keeps the detailed operational budget separate and relies partly on cited or asserted evidence for need, team capacity, and feasibility.
